To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the horse has five ADH isozyme forms (three class I and two class II/III) and four AHD forms (two cytoplasmic and two mitochondrial) and one form of AHR, AOX and XO.

(1) ADH, AHD, AHR, AOX and XOD are widely distributed in equine tissues; (2) AOX and XDO are present only in liver; (3) ADH-C2 is present in all tissues examined; and (4) ADH-C3 is present in most tissues examined.
the horse possesses five isozymic forms of ADH, four of AHD, one of AHR, one of AOX and one of XOX.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the enzymes of the aldoxylase pathway, and their subcellular localization and distribution among the various horse tissues.
the characterization of the major aldehyde metabolizing enzymes in the horse.
the characterization of alcohol dehydro-genase, aldehyde and xanthine dehydrogenases, and aldehyde and x anthine oxidases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
horse liver contains five ADH isozyme forms (three classes), four NAD-dependent AHD isozyme forms, one NADPH-dependent form, one AOX form and one XOX form.
horse liver is a source of multiple ADHs, AHDs, AHRs, AOXs and XOXs.
horse liver contains at least 12 different isozymes of alcohol dehydro-genases and aldehyde dehydro-genases, and at least 2 isozymes of aldehyde oxidases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distribution of ADH isozyme patterns is similar in horse, human and pig, but differs from that of the rat.

(i) ADH-C2 and ADH-B2 are the first examples of class II and class III ADHs reported in horse; (ii) the presence of a novel form of AHR activity in liver is reported; (iii) AHD-1 and AOX are the first enzymes of their type to be reported in horse.
, in addition to the five isoenzymes of ADH, there are at least four isoenzymes for AHD, one for AHR, one for AOX and one for XOX in the horse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the horse is a good model for the study of alcohol and drug metabolism.
the horse liver has a high capacity for ethanol metabolism and that this is reflected in the distribution of ADH isozyme forms in this organ.
the distribution of these enzymes in the tissues of the horse is similar to that observed in humans and other animals.
